# Code of Conduct

This repository follows the
[Code of Conduct: EGI Community](https://www.egi.eu/community-code-of-conduct),
which applies to everyone taking part in EGI activities, including collaborative
platforms such as this repository. Its Sections 1 to 10 are reproduced below
from version 1.0 of 12 October 2026 (EGI Council Policy 10). The version on
egi.eu prevails.

## In this repository

The maintainers uphold the Code here, as Section 7.2 asks of those who run an
EGI space. They may hide, edit or delete comments, lock a conversation, and
block a person from the repository. A block is a removal, so it is reported to
[conduct@egi.eu](mailto:conduct@egi.eu).

To raise a concern, contact a maintainer, or write to
[conduct@egi.eu](mailto:conduct@egi.eu) at any time.

## 1. Preamble

EGI is committed to providing safe, inclusive, and productive environments for
all participants in EGI activities. Mutual respect, open collaboration, and
professional conduct are essential to the success of the research and innovation
communities that EGI serves. This Code of Conduct establishes the standards of
behaviour expected of all participants in EGI-related activities. It aims to:

- Promote a welcoming and inclusive environment where all participants can
  contribute fully.

- Set clear expectations for professional and respectful conduct.

- Provide accessible mechanisms for reporting concerns and addressing potential
  breaches.

- Protect the safety, dignity, and well-being of all community members.

## 2. Scope

This Code applies to all participants in **EGI coordinated activities** that are
organised, convened, or formally supported by the EGI Foundation, including
activities run jointly with Participants. These include, whether in person or
online:

- Conferences, meetings, webinars, training events, and hackathons.

- Working groups and task forces.

- Collaborative platforms and digital communication channels (mailing lists,
  chats, services, forums, and EGI-related social media).

- Social events organised as part of EGI activities.

- External events where a participant is authorised to represent EGI or to
  present on EGI work.

The Code binds every participant without exception, including attendees,
speakers, sponsors, organisers, volunteers, online contributors, and EGI
Foundation staff and contractors.

Conduct within projects is governed by the applicable consortium agreement,
which may adopt this Code.

## 3. Encouraged Behaviours

All participants in EGI activities are encouraged to:

- **Treat all participants with courtesy, dignity, and respect**, regardless of
  background, identity, or role.

- **Be respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences**,
  recognising that diverse perspectives strengthen the community.

- **Give and accept constructive feedback gracefully**, focusing on the
  substance of ideas and contributions.

- **Take responsibility for your actions and contributions**, including
  acknowledging mistakes and working to repair any harm caused.

- **Respect the personal boundaries of others**, whether in physical settings
  (personal space, physical contact) or online (private messages, contact
  requests).

- **Contribute to a welcoming and inclusive environment**, being mindful that
  words and actions may be interpreted differently across cultures, backgrounds,
  and languages.

- **Use EGI platforms and channels for their intended purpose**, respecting the
  norms and expectations of each space.

- **Respect the privacy of others in online settings**, including by not
  recording, screenshotting, or redistributing content from meetings, chats, or
  forums without the consent of those involved, unless the content is intended
  for public distribution.

- **Maintain professional conduct in online interactions**, including in chat
  messages, forum posts, video calls, and shared documents, applying the same
  standards as in face-to-face settings.

- **Report concerns promptly** through the designated channels described in
  Section 6.

## 4. Unacceptable Behaviours

The following behaviours are unacceptable in all EGI activities and spaces. This
list is illustrative, not exhaustive.

- **Harassment:** unwelcome personal attention, following or stalking (whether
  physical or online), and any conduct that creates a hostile or intimidating
  environment.

- **Discrimination:** demeaning or derogatory remarks or conduct based on
  protected characteristics, including race, ethnicity, national or social
  origin, colour, age, disability, neurodiversity, sex, gender identity or
  expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, language, socio-economic
  position, or other status.

- **Sexual harassment:** unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favours,
  inappropriate sexual comments or imagery, and any other unwelcome conduct of a
  sexual nature.

- **Intimidation and threats:** intimidation, threats, or incitement to violence
  of any kind.

- **Deliberate misgendering:** deliberate misgendering or persistent use of
  names that a person has explicitly asked not to be used.

- **Violation of privacy:** sharing or acting on another person’s private or
  personal information without their explicit consent, including publishing
  private messages, sharing screenshots of private conversations, and
  redistributing recordings not intended for public distribution.

- **Unwanted recording:** taking photographs, video, or audio recordings of
  individuals without their consent, or screenshotting online interactions (such
  as video calls or chat conversations) for the purpose of harassment or public
  shaming.

- **Abuse of authority:** using a position of authority or influence within the
  EGI community to intimidate, coerce, or unfairly disadvantage others.

- **Sustained disruption:** deliberate disruption of presentations, discussions,
  meetings, or other activities, including (in online settings) flooding chat
  channels, repeatedly interrupting speakers, or misusing platform features.

- **Unsolicited commercial communications:** using EGI platforms, channels, or
  events for unsolicited commercial, promotional, or vendor communications
  outside the established norms for that activity.

- **Retaliation:** retaliation against anyone who, in good faith, reports,
  testifies, or cooperates under this Code. See Section 8.

## 5. Acceptable Use of EGI Resources

Participants who are granted access to EGI computing, network, or information
resources (including event Wi-Fi, collaborative platforms, and shared tools)
shall:

- Use resources consistently with their intended purpose and in accordance with
  applicable EGI policies.

- Use resources for lawful purposes only.

- Respect the intellectual property rights of others and maintain the
  confidentiality of information accessed through EGI resources.

- Protect access credentials and not share them with unauthorised persons.

- Report any security incidents or suspected misuse promptly to the relevant EGI
  contact.

Limited personal use of event and collaboration resources, such as event Wi-Fi,
collaborative platforms, and shared tools, is permitted, provided that it is
occasional, of negligible scale, and does not interfere with EGI activities or
the work of others. Personal use shall not be made for commercial gain or
political campaigning and remains subject to the standards of behaviour set out
in Sections 3 and 4 of this Code.

Access to and use of federated EGI infrastructure services is governed by the
[EGI Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use](https://go.egi.eu/aup),
together with any terms accepted on enrolment in a Virtual Organisation. The
personal use allowance in this Section does not extend to those services.

## 6. Reporting

### 6.1 How to Report

Anyone who experiences or witnesses behaviour that goes against this Code, or
has any other concern about conduct, is encouraged to raise it. The quickest way
is to speak to an organiser, session chair or moderator, who can act at once
(Section 7.2). Reports can also be sent at any time to <conduct@egi.eu>.

Every report is acknowledged, and the person who made it is told how it was
handled, as far as confidentiality allows. Where someone's safety is at risk,
those running the activity will help them contact venue security or the police
and stay with them until they feel safe.

### 6.2 What to Include

Where possible, reports should include:

- A description of the incident, including dates, times, and setting (event
  name, online platform, channel, or meeting).

- The names or descriptions of the individuals involved.

- The names of any witnesses.

- Any supporting evidence (e.g. screenshots, messages, links to relevant
  content, recordings).

### 6.3 Confidentiality

All reports will be treated confidentially to the greatest extent possible.
Information will be shared only with those who need to be involved in assessing
and resolving the matter.

### 6.4 Good Faith

Reports should be made in good faith and based on genuine concern. Making a
report that is knowingly false or malicious may itself constitute a breach of
this Code.

## 7. Enforcement

### 7.1 Graduated Enforcement

Where a breach of this Code is established, one or more of the following
measures may be applied, proportionate to the nature and severity of the
conduct:

a. **Correction.** A private communication to the person concerned, clarifying
the nature of the issue and the expected standard of behaviour. No formal record
is created beyond internal notes.

b. **Warning.** A formal written warning specifying the conduct that breached
the Code and the conditions for continued participation. Repeated breaches
following a warning may result in further measures.

c. **Temporary restriction.** Exclusion from specific activities, communication
channels, online platforms, or events for a defined period. This may include
removal of access to mailing lists, chat services, forums, or other EGI
platforms. The terms of the restriction and conditions for reinstatement will be
communicated in writing.

d. **Permanent exclusion.** Removal from all EGI community activities and
platforms, including revocation of access to all online spaces. Permanent
exclusion is reserved for the most serious breaches or for cases where previous
measures have failed to resolve the conduct.

### 7.2 Decision-Making

Those who run an EGI activity or space, such as event organisers, session
chairs, moderators and platform administrators, uphold this Code there. They may
take whatever step is needed to keep the activity safe and productive, from
asking a person to stop to removing them from the session, event or channel.
Such steps apply to that activity only and are not measures under Section 7.1.
Removing a person is reported under Section 6; for other steps, they use their
judgement on whether a report is needed, and most situations are resolved
locally.

Measures under Section 7.1 are decided on a report under Section 6. The EGI
Foundation Director, or a person the Director designates, assesses the report
and hears the person concerned (Section 7.3). Where a breach is established:

a. **Correction or warning.** Decided by the Director.

b. **Temporary restriction.** Decided by the Director together with the
Chairperson of the Executive Board, or with a member of the Executive Board
designated by the Chairperson; where they disagree, the Executive Board decides.

c. **Permanent exclusion.** Decided by the Executive Board on the proposal of
the Director.

Where a restriction is needed without delay, the Director may impose it, and the
joint decision under (b) follows within ten working days. A person who has a
conflict of interest in a case, including the Director or the Chairperson, takes
no part in it, and the Executive Board designates a replacement.

### 7.3 Right to Respond and to Appeal

Decisions on enforcement will be communicated privately to the person concerned.
Before a final decision is taken on any measure beyond a correction, the person
shall have a reasonable opportunity to respond and present their account.

A person subject to a warning or a temporary restriction may appeal in writing
to the Executive Board within twenty working days of being notified of the
decision; a member who took part in the decision takes no part in the appeal,
and the decision of the Executive Board is final.

### 7.4 Records

A record of formal enforcement actions (warnings, temporary restrictions, and
permanent exclusions) shall be maintained by the EGI Foundation in accordance
with its data protection policies. The Director reports formal enforcement
actions to the Executive Board at its next meeting, in a form that protects the
confidentiality of those involved.

## 8. Non-Retaliation

Anyone who reports a concern, provides information during an investigation, or
cooperates with an enforcement process in good faith shall not face adverse
consequences as a result. The EGI Foundation will take reasonable steps to
protect those individuals.

## 9. Relationship to Other Documents

This Code of Conduct complements and should be read in conjunction with:

- [EGI Foundation Statutes (2015)](https://go.egi.eu/statutes).

- [EGI Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use](https://www.egi.eu/terms-of-use/).

- [EGI Privacy Policy](https://www.egi.eu/privacy-notice/).

Where there is any inconsistency between this Code and the Statutes, the
Statutes shall prevail. Where there is any inconsistency between this Code and
the EGI Acceptable Use Policy and Conditions of Use, or other service-specific
conditions of use, those documents shall prevail in respect of the use of the
resources and services they govern.

Members of the Governance Bodies are bound by the Code of Conduct “EGI
Governance” for conduct in the exercise of their governance role, and by this
Code as participants in all other EGI activities. A report under Section 6 that
concerns a Member acting in a governance role is referred to the Chairperson of
the relevant Governance Body and handled under that Code.

## 10. Entry into Force, Publication and Review

<!-- textlint-disable terminology -->

This Code enters into force on the date of its adoption. It is published on the
EGI website and referenced in the registration terms of EGI events and in the
terms of use of EGI online spaces; taking part in an EGI activity implies
acceptance of this Code.

<!-- textlint-enable terminology -->

This Code shall be reviewed at least once every three years, or sooner if
circumstances require. Proposed amendments shall be submitted to the Council for
approval in accordance with the procedures for amending Council policies.
